sources.population: Athletes 18–35, sport>=3/week, clinical+ultrasound PT, VISA-P<80; median 2-year symptoms; 76%male. Acute injury, rupture and other pathology excluded.
sources.comparator: Pain-provoking 25-degree decline eccentric squat twice daily 12 weeks, then sport-specific work; different progression.
sources.coInterventions: Both: education, activity modification, hip/calf/core/flexibility work; no reported extra treatment.
sources.outcomes: 24-week VISA-P improvement 28 vs 18; adjusted MD 9 (95%CI 1, 16). Return-preinjury-sport 43% vs 27%, p.13; adherence 40% vs 49%, p.33.
sources.uncertainty: Unblinded patients; missing-data sensitivity; mostly chronic young athletes; individual component not isolated.
sources.harms: No serious exercise events; two ankle sprains during sport.
sources.limitations: Unblinded patients; missing-data sensitivity; mostly chronic young athletes; individual component not isolated.

protocol.execution: Single-leg machine leg-press/extension; sequential isometric, isotonic, energy-storage, sport stages.
protocol.dose: Stage 1: 5x 45 s at 60-degree flexion, 70%MVC. Stage 2: 4x 15(10–60 degrees) progressing 4x 6(almost 0–90). Stage 3: 3x 10 bilateral to 6x 10 unilateral jumps.
protocol.frequency: Isometric daily; isotonic alternate days; energy-storage every third day; sport every 2–3 days; maintenance 2/week.
protocol.supervision: Unsupervised, physician instruction, video/brochure; gym reimbursement.
protocol.progression: Pain<=3/10 on single-leg squat and>=1 week at stage before next; increase load/range in stage 2.
protocol.stoppingRules: Reduce/avoid considerable-pain sport>=4 weeks; acceptable pain<=3/10 in this study. Not a universal app threshold.

locations: Results > Clinical outcomes; Adverse events; Discussion > limitations

sources.design: Multidisciplinary guideline, onlineJuly 2024, journal 2025; systematic reviews+RCTs, GRADE, informal consensus.
sources.population: Clinically distinguished PFP and PT; not generic anterior knee pain; nonoperative initial management.
sources.comparator: Exercise and multiple additional conservative treatments.
sources.coInterventions: Education/loading advice; additional treatment decisions after response review.
sources.outcomes: PFP: quadriceps/hip exercise 6–12 weeks; reconsider diagnosis if no improvement 12 weeks. PT: progressive quadriceps resistance>=12 weeks; heavy-slow preferred with alternate contractions for reactivity; review if no meaningful change 12 weeks.
sources.followUp: Recommended 6/12-week reassessment, not a trial follow-up.
sources.uncertainty: Evidence low/very-low; exercise reporting incomplete; informal consensus; scheduled guideline review after 2027, not automatic currentness guarantee.
sources.harms: Harms inconsistently reported; survey pain worsening is not randomized harm evidence.
sources.limitations: Evidence low/very-low; exercise reporting incomplete; informal consensus; scheduled guideline review after 2027, not automatic currentness guarantee.

protocol.execution: PFP: quadriceps/hip; PT: education/loading, strength, energy-storage, maintenance.
protocol.dose: No universal sets/reps/load; PT>=12 weeks strength, PFP 6–12 weeks.
protocol.supervision: PFP preferably partly PT-supervised; individualized management.
protocol.progression: Adjust intensity to pain; stage PT toward sport-dependent plyometrics then maintenance.
protocol.stoppingRules: No universal numeric threshold; reassess poor response after 12 weeks.

exerciseMappings.matchRationale: Catalog leg-extension is dynamic weight_reps with repetition progression; it does not encode MVC-calibrated sustained force or fixed knee angle. A duration/force clinical identity is required; not equivalent to generic5-second progression.

Catalog leg-press has generic Machine/weight_reps and routine progression; no documented equivalence to this unilateral stage-specific range. Preserve alternative to knee-extension machine, not a mandatory sequence between machines.

proposedRules.statement: Retain separate isometric and isotonic loading candidates for independent clinical review within a pain-monitored staged program. Do not import trial pain criteria, loads or return-to-sport timing as defaults.
